# Set81 retained-admission public evidence

This is a source-only schema for the root-owned actual run. No file described here is an existing successful result. `check(owned, case, command_pid)` must return the complete absolute public-file identity map; never recurse into `private-fixture`, wallet, outbox or database directories.

The helper is limited to the original 900-second context, 1080-second outer capture and 180 generated blocks. Both cases require two accepted canonical pool receipts and two rewards. The independently qualified selection is `inputs/reference-v1.json`, 174293 bytes, SHA256 `17557b28921290461fdf47b9ed6f1b800d3d077ee5d325a4ec59277ab3faca6a`. The payout is 1,980,000,000 atoms, fee209 and change19,999,791. Actual TLS/port/due fields are selected once by the inherited helper; only maintenance1000 and its dependent selected IDs differ from the earlier public recipe.

All phase JSON is ordinary public Go JSON plus newline. Required fields in the new literal maps are always present, including null response/error pointers. Original reused types keep their original tags. The executable type declarations are the exact schema authority; this document names their crosslinks.

`target` is the exact `admissionTarget` struct in admission_relay.go: request_id; complete original work; proof; authorization; receipt accepted_sequence2; first_receipt accepted_sequence1; original inserted first_admission; exact admission request body SHA; first held timestamp. Target is selected by the accepted receipt, not HTTP arrival ordinal. Both receipts must be actual block winners and their headers/hash/job match the original work and proof. The target request body is unchanged in every target event. Other prospect-only requests may exist and are audited, not represented as a global two-birth restriction.

`audit` is `retainedAdmissionAudit`. It carries the full financial/source/round/issuer audit, exact target job/proof/auth and optional immutable record, target record/index/outbox/signed-admission/publication counts, complete global census/issuer row hashes/public-file before/after identities. Ownership outbox rows are permanent: A target_outbox remains1 after publication; B remains0. Final A requires one exact published target; B requires no target record or ownership evidence. Original full audits remain the authority; the checker does not claim to reproduce Argon2 or signatures in Python.

`tls_relay` is `admissionRelayEvidence` emitted only after original listener and every handler join. It has version1, max_events512, complete target, final mode, lost bool/optional lost_response, bounded ordered events, failure/closed/handlers_joined. Each event has its original path, start/end times, public request ID/job/header and exact request byte count/hash; target/mode; held/deadline/released/forwarded times; upstream status/response byte count/hash; lost/downstream/context/failure; typed admission or api_error. No credentials, raw headers or opaque errors are included. Canonical response byte hashes use the original actual forwarded bytes (production canonical JSON plus LF). Target holds are at most10000ms and bounded by original expiry. Initial retain is canceled before forwarding. In A only loss mode is explicitly released; a genuine inserted success is withheld by closing the original TLS connection before headers, and subsequent retries are held until CLI joins. Historical replay is forwarded normally and exact immutable Record is checked. B terminal expired must be actual HTTP409, version3, code expired, outcome_unknown false after original expiry. Busy or other genuine refusals do not fabricate completion.

Generation names are fixed. All cases have operator-init, operator-rotate-pool-0, operator-rotate-pool-1 and operator-rotate-admission commands, then original serve lifetimes. A uses operator-serve-1/2/3 and cli-1/2/3; B uses operator-serve-1/2 and cli-1/2. Each CLI is signaled once and must exit0 with empty stderr and joined pipes. Every serve is joined before its closed root audit. No intentional SIGKILL/crash path is used. Dated public operator status—not an injected readiness getter—proves source full, reason pool_capacity, original ordinary maximum2, public Ready, no PublicCode/RoundCode, Through2/Rounds2. Initial held CLI is joined before waiting for status; every reopened serve reaches fresh readiness before another CLI starts.

Exact public process logs are the fixed stdout/stderr names written by original `operator_process.go`, `cli_process.go` and node helpers. Select names explicitly from those declarations/generation names, not by recursive tree discovery. The helper appends no new source jobs/work after the initial full-source audit. Unrelated terminal request rows may consume remaining finite q budget; all counts are retained and reported, while this target's completed request/result stays byte-identical. The stopped controller reopening after delivery must preserve the entire original outbox row/control snapshot through payment.

The phase04 `response` and `api_error` pointers are independent last observations within the final armed generation, not a mutually exclusive last-outcome pair. Both reset at arm; a genuine Busy followed by successful historical delivery may leave both nonnull. Bind each nonnull value to its matching target event, and require the final actual successful/expired event plus durable exact target state separately. `first_held_at_ms` is sampled when the target is first captured and is at or before the first event held_at_ms; equality is not asserted.
